title: docs(qa): 18.0 sweep anchor round 13 — QA round 3 surface:cli findings in cli.json, plus three carried items
body:
Refs #24579

Clause-②: no

Round 13 of the 18.0 sweep's wave anchor (claim `6288038866`, PM loop round 22). It covers QA round 3's `surface:cli` checklist-accuracy findings C1–C9 (QA record #24786) and B6 (QA record #24787) in `cli.json`, plus three items carried on the anchor. Only checklist text changes. Twelve items in three area files (`cli.json` 9, `access-security.json` 2, `approvals.json` 1) each take one `revision` bump and one `history` row naming the record and the finding. There is no product code, test, pin, changeset text or `RUNNER.md` change.

Every finding was re-read in the code at base `7697ddcf94` before it was written, and all of them hold. Every source cited below is byte-identical at the merged `origin/main` `5cb6e6e0aa`. A scripted textual editor made the edits: it re-parses each area file and asserts that only the target items changed, and in each of them only the declared fields, plus `revision` (+1) and one appended `history` row. The raw file is never re-serialized.

### Carried item 11 — the governing-text decision

The rule applied: governing text decides a clause, and a clause is re-scoped only where an ADR, spec docblock or AGENTS.md rule states the answer. ADR-0131 D7 states the attribution reading. `sys_audit_log` is deployment-level state with no organization column. The organization a row is about "becomes a plain attribution field under a name the tenant-field resolver does not claim, never the tenancy anchor". Such objects "are governed by object permission, not by the wall". D9 scopes the no-NULL rule to tenant-column objects ("column ⇒ in scope"). This moves acceptance[4]'s premise: its "invisible to RLS readers" was written for #8245, when the ledger was walled. It does not answer the question, though. No ADR states that a member-less actor's audit row may carry a NULL attribution, and none states that the platform operator reads such rows. The operator's 200 and the user's 403 that QA run #24783 measured come from the implementation: the object's `defaultRowScope` `tenant_id == current_user.organization_id`, which a NULL row matches for no organization reader. So the clause stays as written, and knownGaps[3] gains the D7 reading. This falsifies the dispatch's hypothesis 2 in its conclusion: D7 does state the attribution reading, but not the two facts an alignment needs.

## Items left alone, with reasons

- `access-security.no-active-org-session-semantics` acceptance[4]: kept as written, by the decision above.
- `cli.hook-body-extraction-gates` steps[0] and acceptance[0].verify still say "fourteen at base 9a7838edf5". `FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS` still holds 14 entries at `7697ddcf94`, so both are true as dated readings.
- `cli.dev-boot-contract` acceptance[0] (clause, verify, evidence): unchanged. Its console leg stands; the new requires[2] says what the leg needs and how to record it when the Console is unbuilt.
- `cli.build-own-contract` acceptance[0]'s success key list: unchanged. B6 names only acceptance[3], and QA run #24787 scored acceptance[0] a pass.
- PM hypothesis 1 (a roster constant can replace each count): it holds for C7, where `FORBIDDEN_PATTERNS` is a declared array and is now the anchor. It does not hold for C6: doctor has no row roster, because its rows are pushed inline in `run()`. That verify now names the push sites and checks, and states no count.

## Gates

The derived list is `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, computed on the actual change set: 3 paths vs merge base `5cb6e6e0aa`, 118 changed lines. It gives 13 commands. Each one ran at head `b66554b1ad`, with its exit code captured before any pipe, and each exited 0:

`pnpm check:platform-checklist` · `pnpm check:nul-bytes` · `pnpm check:doc-authoring` · `pnpm check:cross-package-test-inputs` · `pnpm check:driver-memory-census` · `pnpm check:gitlink-declared` · `pnpm check:refd-timer-probe` · `pnpm check:watch-hint-literal` · `pnpm --filter @objectstack/lint run check:doc-formula-expressions` (after a locked `turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/lint... --concurrency=2`) · `node scripts/check-ci-filter-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs` · `node scripts/check-closing-keyword-parity.mjs --self-test` · `node scripts/check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`

The `--ran` reconciliation reads "13 derived, 13 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN", a derived zero because all 13 recorded an exit code. No per-PR CI job runs `pnpm check:platform-checklist`, so this local reading is its evidence:

| reading | base `7697ddcf94` | head `b66554b1ad` |
|:--|:--|:--|
| items | 16 areas, 328 items | 16 areas, 328 items |
| line citations | 0 survive across 21 swept documents | 0 survive across 21 swept documents |
| symbol anchors | 954/964 resolved, 10 on the named residual, 18 file floors held | 965/975 resolved, 10 on the named residual, 18 file floors held |

The history rows' `ref` are written as this PR's number in the commit that follows this PR's creation. That commit changes only those twelve strings, and the gate readings at that final head are in the report on #24579.

Serial check: `origin/main` was merged before this PR was opened. None of the 14 open PRs touches `cli.json`, `access-security.json` or `approvals.json`, or any `docs/qa/` path, so no `git merge-tree` probe was owed.

Changeset: `docs/qa/**` ships in no package. No public package's `files[]` names it, and the root package is private. So this PR carries `skip-changeset` and touches no `.changeset/*.md`.

## Acceptance notes

- The load-time refusal payload of `os build --json` and `os validate --json` carries the error's message and `code`, but not the structured zod `issues`. The `STACK_SCHEMA_INVALID` ledger row (`packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts`) says that error carries them, and `errorCodeFields` copies only `code` and `httpStatus`. The message renders those issues as text: the `StackSchemaInvalidError` docblock in `packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts` says "the message already renders those, and the envelope's job is the machine-readable half". The CLI payload declares no `issues` key, so this is not a breach of a declared contract. It is recorded in `cli.build-own-contract` knownGaps[0] and filed nowhere (carrier: none).
